content: The text provided is a list of references from various studies, articles, and clinical trials related to antiretroviral therapy (ART) for HIV treatment. These references include detailed citations of research on drug efficacy, safety, pharmacokinetics, resistance, and treatment strategies for both adults and children living with HIV. 1. De Luca et al. (2013) explored strategies for sequencing antiretroviral treatments to address HIV-1 drug resistance in adolescents and adults in lowand middle-income countries. Their findings were published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases. 2. Barnhart and Shelton (2015) discussed the next generation of antiretroviral drugs and emphasized the importance of collaborative efforts to advance HIV treatment. This was published in Global Health Science and Practice. 3. Paton et al. (2014), on behalf of the EARNEST Trial Team, assessed second-line antiretroviral regimens for HIV therapy in Africa. Their results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 4. Amin et al. (2015) conducted a randomized open-label study comparing raltegravir to nucleoside-based regimens in second-line therapy with lopinavir/ritonavir over 96 weeks. The study demonstrated non-inferiority of raltegravir and was published in PLoS One. 5. McKeage et al. (2009) reviewed the use of darunavir in managing HIV infection in adults, highlighting its efficacy and safety. This review was published in the journal Drugs. 6. Deeks (2014) provided an updated review of darunavir's role in managing HIV-1 infection, focusing on its clinical applications and outcomes. This was also published in Drugs. 7. Khan et al. (2014) reported on second-line treatment failures and initial experiences with third-line antiretroviral therapy in Mumbai, India. Their findings were published in Global Health Action. 8. Ford et al. (2013) discussed the optimization and simplification of antiretroviral therapy for adults and children, emphasizing the need for accessible and effective treatment regimens. This was published in Current Opinion in HIV/AIDS. 9. The World Health Organization (2015) conducted a systematic review to inform guidelines on switching ART regimens when treatment failure occurs. This review was part of the WHO Consolidated Guidelines. 10. Bunupuradah et al. (2012) compared second-line lopinavir/ritonavir monotherapy to a combination regimen including tenofovir and lamivudine in patients failing NNRTI regimens. This study, known as the HIV STAR study, was published in Antiviral Therapy. 11. Ciaffi et al. (2015), on behalf of the 2LADY study group, evaluated the efficacy and safety of three second-line antiretroviral regimens in HIV-infected patients in Africa. Their results were published in AIDS. 12. Laker et al. (2014) compared boosted lopinavir to boosted atazanavir in patients failing NNRTI-based first-line regimens in an urban clinic in Kampala. This study was published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society. 13. Patel et al. (2011) compared the effectiveness of low-dose indinavir/ritonavir versus atazanavir/ritonavir-based generic ART in NNRTI-experienced HIV-1-infected patients in India. Their findings were published in the Journal of the International Association of Physicians in AIDS Care. 14. The SECOND-LINE Study Group (2013) conducted a randomized, open-label, non-inferiority study comparing ritonavir-boosted lopinavir with nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors versus raltegravir in adults with virological failure of a standard first-line ART regimen. This study was published in The Lancet. 15. Katlama et al. (2007) reported 24-week results of the POWER 1 trial, which evaluated the efficacy and safety of TMC114/ritonavir in treatment-experienced HIV patients. This was published in AIDS. 16. Haubrich et al. (2007) presented 24-week efficacy and safety data for TMC114/ritonavir in treatment-experienced HIV patients. Their findings were published in AIDS. 17. Cahn et al. (2011) analyzed once-daily versus twice-daily darunavir/ritonavir in treatment-experienced HIV-1-infected patients over 48 weeks. This study was published in AIDS. 18. Madruga et al. (2007) compared the efficacy and safety of darunavir/ritonavir to lopinavir/ritonavir at 48 weeks in treatment-experienced HIV-infected patients in the TITAN trial. This was published in The Lancet. 19. Moltó et al. (2015) demonstrated that a reduced darunavir dose is as effective as the standard dose in maintaining HIV suppression in virologically suppressed patients. This randomized clinical trial was published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy. 20. The WHO Consolidated Guidelines (2015) provided comprehensive recommendations on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection. 21. Acosta et al. (2007) investigated the pharmacokinetics and safety of atazanavir administered twice daily with rifampin. Their findings were published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy. 22. Burger et al. (2006) studied the effect of rifampin on the steady-state pharmacokinetics of atazanavir with ritonavir in healthy volunteers. This was published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy. 23. Justesen et al. (2004) examined the pharmacokinetic interaction between rifampin and the combination of indinavir and low-dose ritonavir in HIV-infected patients. Their study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 24. La Porte et al. (2004) evaluated the pharmacokinetics of adjusted-dose lopinavir/ritonavir combined with rifampin in healthy volunteers. This study was published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy. 25. The Panel on Antiretroviral Guidelines for Adults and Adolescents (2015) provided guidelines for the use of antiretroviral agents in HIV-1-infected adults and adolescents. 26. Mudzviti et al. (2015) reported on the use of rifabutin for treating tuberculosis in HIV-infected adults receiving boosted protease inhibitor-containing ART regimens, highlighting experiences of neutropenia. This was presented at the Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections. 27. Nijland et al. (2008) observed a high incidence of adverse events in healthy volunteers receiving rifampicin and adjusted doses of lopinavir/ritonavir tablets. Their findings were published in AIDS. 28. Decloedt et al. (2011) studied the pharmacokinetics of lopinavir in HIV-infected adults receiving rifampin with adjusted doses of lopinavir/ritonavir tablets. This was published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy. 29. Dore et al. (2010) reported frequent hepatitis B virus rebound among HIV-HBV co-infected patients following ART interruption in the SMART study. This was published in AIDS. 30. Wenning et al. (2009) examined the effect of rifampin, a potent inducer of drug-metabolizing enzymes, on the pharmacokinetics of raltegravir. Their findings were published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy. 31. Dooley et al. (2012) outlined pharmacology research priorities for TB and HIV therapeutics. This was published in AIDS Research and Treatment. 32. Penazzato et al. (2015) discussed optimizing drugs to achieve treatment targets for children and adolescents living with HIV. This was published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society. 33. Lazarus et al. (2015) reviewed secondand third-line ART options for children and adolescents, presenting their findings at the 7th International Workshop on HIV Pediatrics. 34. Zanoni et al. (2012) analyzed pediatric responses to second-line ART in South Africa. Their findings were published in PLoS One. 35. Orrell et al. (2013) investigated resistance in pediatric patients experiencing virologic failure with firstand second-line ART. This was published in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal. 36. Van Zyl et al. (2009) studied protease inhibitor resistance in South African children with virologic failure. Their findings were published in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal. 37. Meyers et al. (2015) reported virologic failure among children taking lopinavir/ritonavir-containing first-line ART in South Africa. This was published in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal. 38. Taylor et al. (2011) observed rapid development of antiretroviral drug resistance mutations in HIV-infected children under two years of age initiating protease inhibitor-based therapy in South Africa. This was published in AIDS Research and Human Retroviruses. 39. Bailey et al. (2015) assessed the safety of atazanavir and darunavir in pediatric cohorts in Europe and Thailand, presenting their findings at the 19th International Workshop on HIV Observational Databases. 40. Götte et al. (2000) demonstrated that the M184V mutation in HIV-1 reverse transcriptase impairs the rescue of chain-terminated DNA synthesis. This was published in the Journal of Virology. 41. Ajose et al. (2012) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of treatment outcomes for patients on second-line ART in resource-limited settings. This was published in AIDS. 42. Pozniak et al. (2008) evaluated the effect of baseline viral susceptibility on response to darunavir/ritonavir versus control protease inhibitors in treatment-experienced HIV-1-infected patients. This was published in AIDS Research and Human Retroviruses. 43. Steigbigel et al. (2008) studied raltegravir with optimized background therapy for resistant HIV-1 infection. Their findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 44. Schiller and Youssef-Bessler (2009) reviewed etravirine, a second-generation NNRTI active against NNRTI-resistant strains of HIV. This was published in Clinical Therapeutics. 45. Gatell et al. (2010) reported long-term efficacy and safety of raltegravir in patients with limited treatment options in a Phase II study. This was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 46. Steigbigel et al. (2010) presented long-term efficacy and safety data for raltegravir combined with optimized background therapy in treatment-experienced patients with drug-resistant HIV. This was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 47. Katlama et al. (2010) evaluated the efficacy and safety of etravirine at week 96 in treatment-experienced HIV-1-infected patients in the DUET-1 and DUET-2 trials. This was published in Antiviral Therapy. 48. Fagard et al. (2012) reported long-term efficacy and safety of raltegravir, etravirine, and darunavir/ritonavir in treatment-experienced patients in the ANRS 139 TRIO trial. This was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 49. Cahn et al. (2013) compared dolutegravir to raltegravir in antiretroviral-experienced, integrase inhibitor-naive adults with HIV. This was published in The Lancet. 50. Capetti et al. (2014) presented four years of data on raltegravir-based salvage therapy in treatment-experienced HIV-1-infected patients in the SALIR-E Study. This was published in the International Journal of Antimicrobial Agents. 51. Gazzola et al. (2014) evaluated the efficacy and safety of darunavir/ritonavir plus etravirine dual regimens in antiretroviral therapy-experienced patients. This was published in HIV Clinical Trials. 52. Arathoon et al. (2014) presented week 48 results of a Phase IV trial of etravirine with antiretrovirals other than darunavir/ritonavir in treatment-experienced adults. This was published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society. 53. Castagna et al. (2014) reported 24-week results of the VIKING-3 Study, evaluating dolutegravir in antiretroviral-experienced patients with raltegravirand/or elvitegravir-resistant HIV-1. This was published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases. 54. Vingerhoets et al. (2015) assessed the efficacy of etravirine combined with darunavir or other ritonavir-boosted protease inhibitors in HIV-1-infected patients. This observational study used pooled European cohort data and was published in HIV Medicine. 55. Prado et al. (2005) studied HIV-1 fitness evolution in antiretroviral-experienced patients with sustained CD4+ T cell counts but persistent virologic failure. This was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 56. Fox et al. (2006) conducted the COLATE trial, evaluating continuation versus discontinuation of lamivudine in individuals failing a lamivudine-containing regimen. This was published in Antiviral Therapy. 57. Tashima et al. (2013) presented findings from the ACTG OPTIONS Study, which demonstrated that omitting NRTIs from ART regimens is not inferior to adding NRTIs in treatment-experienced HIV+ subjects failing a protease inhibitor regimen. This was presented at the 20th Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections. 58. Imaz et al. (2011) evaluated the efficacy and safety of NRTI-sparing salvage therapy for multidrug-resistant HIV-1 infection based on new-class and new-generation antiretrovirals. This was published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy. 59. Di Biagio et al. (2011) examined the use of nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors in salvage therapy for treatment-experienced patients. This was part of the CISAI Group's research.
